text:
Alex: FYI customer `acme-payments` just opened a P1 — their tool/function calls started failing after we promoted model v3.2 to canary yesterday.
Jamie: Can you paste the error they see?
Alex: Shortened: API 200 but no tool execution. Their webhook never gets called. Our logs show schema validation error from our function-caller layer.
Alex: Example payload they sent (sanitized):
```json
{
  "input": "get balance for acct 123",
  "model": "redwood-instruct-v3.2",
  "functions": [
    {
      "name": "get_user_balance",
      "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "account_id": {"type": "string"}
        },
        "required": ["account_id"]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
Alex: Their server responded with our service's parsed function call but `arguments` were rejected when hitting their webhook: 
```json
{
  "tool_call": {
    "name": "GetUserBalance",
    "arguments": "\"accountId\": 123\n"
  }
}
```
Jamie: Aha — note the function name casing. The model returned `GetUserBalance` and a malformed arguments string (not valid JSON). That would break our tool dispatcher which expects exact name + JSON args.
Maria: Do we see this only on v3.2 canary? Previous v3.1 returned `get_user_balance` and proper JSON args.
Alex: Correct — logs correlate to requests routed to v3.2 canary pool only. We have 18 distinct customer reports so far (mix of enterprise + small). Usually a single canary host but this looks widespread within the canary cohort.
Sami: Could be model tokenizer/decoding change or new function-calling shaping. Any diffs in our function-calling shim? Ops-bot deployed runtime patch yesterday but that was only perf flags.
Jamie: I pulled request traces: all affected requests used our new model variant `redwood-instruct-v3.2` and the responses have `tool_call.name` with inconsistent casing and `tool_call.arguments` as plain text in some cases. Example from our API logs:
```
[2026-03-15T21:07:12Z] req=abcd123 model=redwood-instruct-v3.2 -> tool_call.name=GetUserBalance tool_call.arguments=accountId: 123
```
Maria: That stringified args looks like the model serialized args in free text instead of JSON. Could be decoding sampler or instruction prompt change.
Alex: Customer repro steps they shared:
1) Send same request against v3.1 -> success, webhook receives proper JSON args, tool invoked.
2) Send against v3.2 canary -> API returns tool_call but args malformed and tool not invoked.
3) They tried setting `function_call: \"none\"` and fallback to parsing — fails as well.
Sami: For mitigation we can 1) pin affected customers to v3.1, 2) add a temporary tolerant parser that attempts to fix common formats (snake/camel/case & colon-delimited) before rejecting, 3) rollback canary if patch not ready.
Jamie: Ops: can we pin `acme-payments` and the other 17 customers off the canary pool now? Prefer automated customer pinning for speed.
ops-bot: pinned 18 customers to `redwood-instruct-v3.1` (actioned by Sami) — ticket #INC-2026-042 created.
Maria: Also adding strict schema validation to the canary monitoring alerts so we detect non-JSON arguments ASAP.
Alex: Customer asked for ETA — they depend on tool calls for payments so high severity. We should offer immediate rollback to all canary traffic if we can't get a fix in <4 hours.
Jamie: Root cause hypotheses: (A) model generation changed naming convention for function names (PascalCase vs snake_case) and (B) generation of `arguments` switched from JSON to free-form text due to new system prompt tuning in v3.2.
Sami: Quick test: sending synthetic prompt to v3.2 in our staging shows the same behavior. I'll run a small eval over 200 function-calling prompts to quantify failure rate and common patterns.
Maria: If failure rate >5% we should rollback. Ops, prioritize rollback plan and runbooks.
ops-bot: rollback runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/model_rollbacks — standby.
Jamie: I'll draft a safe short-term shim: if `arguments` isn't parseable JSON, try heuristics: replace `\n` with `,`, wrap keys in quotes, convert `accountId` -> `account_id` mapping table for popular APIs, then validate against function schema. This is not perfect but canbuy us time.
Alex: Keep the customer updated: told them we're investigating, pinned them to v3.1, and will follow up with either a patch or rollback within 4 hours.
Sami: Update: after 30m run, failure rate is 23% across the sample and patterns include PascalCase names and colon-delimited args. Not acceptable for canary.
Jamie: Recommendation: rollback v3.2 from canary now and freeze rollout until model team provides a fix. Notify partners and open a postmortem.
Maria: I'll create a dedicated incident channel and start the customer comms template.
Alex: Thanks. Assigning owners: Sami (investigate model/system prompt changes), Jamie (shim + short-term tolerant parser), Maria (customer comms + incident channel), Ops (rollback if needed).
Sami: Rolling back canary per Jamie's rec — initiating now.
ops-bot: Rollback started for `redwood-instruct-v3.2` canary cohort. ETA ~ 18 minutes.
Alex: Will update customer when rollback completes. Good call everyone. :thumbsup:
